title: "Errata"

format:
  pdf:
    output-file: blair_coppock_moor_2020_errata.pdf
    geometry: margin=1.25in
    fontsize: 11pt

The maintained replication code behind these errata is at <https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/blair_coppock_moor_2020> and is archived at Zenodo at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24168286>, a DOI that always resolves to the latest version.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

meta <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "figure_4_meta_estimates.csv"),
                 show_col_types = FALSE)
thresholds <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "text_power_thresholds.csv"),
                       show_col_types = FALSE)
published <- read_csv(here("ground_truth", "published_claims.csv"),
                      col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

# Every number inside a corrected sentence below is computed here, from the deposited
# data, at the time this document is rendered. That includes the numbers that were not
# wrong: a token carried over from the published sentence is inherited on trust, and
# rendering the whole sentence from the pipeline is what verifies it. A number an entry
# does not correct is rendered at the precision the page prints it, so it reproduces the
# published token exactly, and the check after the spine refuses to render if it does not.
meta_row <- function(subset_id, which_row) {
  rows <- meta[meta$subset == subset_id & meta$row == which_row, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(rows) == 1)
  rows
}

mu <- function(subset_id, column = "estimate") {
  100 * meta_row(subset_id, "Random effects meta-analysis")[[column]]
}

ppi <- function(subset_id, column) {
  100 * meta_row(subset_id, "Predictive Intervals (50% and 95%)")[[column]]
}

# The two summary rows sit in every subset, so the study count is what is left over.
n_studies <- function(subset_id) sum(meta$subset == subset_id) - 2L

curve <- function(size) {
  value <- thresholds$value_points[
    thresholds$claim == str_glue(
      "Figure 2a: bias at which RMSE of list equals RMSE of direct, N = {size}"
    )
  ]
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  value
}

# One decimal place on the percentage-point scale for a corrected figure, and the article's
# own en dash for the minus sign, so a corrected sentence reads like the published one.
pts <- function(x) str_replace(sprintf("%.1f", x), "^-", "–")

# Whole points, for a figure the entry does not correct: the precision the page prints.
pts0 <- function(x) str_replace(sprintf("%.0f", x), "^-", "–")

# The same figure as a plain number for corrected_values, with an ASCII minus a parser can
# read in place of the article's en dash.
ascii_minus <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "–", "-")

# Fuller precision, for a reason line rather than a sentence.
pts2 <- function(x) str_replace(sprintf("%.2f", x), "^-", "–")

# The article's own Table 4 cell for the same quantity, quoted from the extraction of the
# published page rather than retyped here.
table4 <- function(claim_id) {
  str_replace(published$value_paper[published$claim_id == claim_id], "^-", "–")
}
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from this tibble into
# this document and into the machine-readable errata_entries.csv written at the bottom of
# the file, which is what any other document carrying these corrections reads. Before the
# spine existed an entry was written out in prose wherever it was needed, and the copies
# had already diverged.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be set by any of them.
#
# Numbering follows PROCEDURES.md Stage 4b: entries are ordered by severity block (quantity;
# description, interpretation, definition; label, float, cross_reference; wording, spelling,
# typography; bibliographic), discovery order inside a block, and a finding that lands in an
# earlier block renumbers the entries after it. Renumbered 2026-11-07; the old-to-new map is
# in that day's commit message.
#
# A published or corrected value that the pipeline computes stays computed: the field is
# built with str_glue() so the number is produced when this document renders, not typed.
#
# claim_ids is the semicolon-separated list of ground-truth claim_id values the entry
# corrects, and it is what makes "is this finding published?" a query rather than a reading
# of every note. It is empty where an entry has no ground-truth row, which is normal for a
# bibliographic or structural entry. ground_truth/build_ground_truth.R refuses to build if
# any id here is absent from the ground truth.
#
# corrected_values runs parallel to claim_ids, one value per id in the same order, carrying
# the corrected quantity as a number rather than as a sentence. The sentence already holds
# it, but only inside prose a reader has to parse. Each value comes from the same expression
# that glues the sentence, so the two cannot be written apart, and the gate below re-checks
# that each one is still inside the span it belongs to. An entry of a class that changes no
# quantity carries NA, and so does a note-form entry, which corrects nothing.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  1, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The sexual orientation underreporting estimate carries the wrong sign",
  "Results",
  "For questions thought to be subject to overreporting, the average estimate of sensitivity bias is –2 percentage points; for underreporting, the estimate is [[+2]] percentage points.",
  str_glue("For questions thought to be subject to overreporting, the average estimate of sensitivity bias is {pts0(mu('g6'))} percentage points; for underreporting, the estimate is [[{pts(mu('g7'))}]] percentage points."),
  str_glue(
    "Table 4 prints {table4('t4_g7_mu_estimate')} for the same quantity. The paper's ",
    "conclusion for this literature, that sensitivity bias in questions about attitudes ",
    "towards gays and lesbians cannot be distinguished from zero, is unaffected."),
  "so_under_mu",
  ascii_minus(str_glue("{pts(mu('g7'))}")),

  2, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The racial prejudice 95 per cent predictive interval",
  "Results",
  "The 50% predictive interval reaches from +1 to +7 points, but the 95% predictive interval admits large negative biases ([[–16]] points) to large positive biases up to [[16]] points.",
  str_glue("The 50% predictive interval reaches from +{pts0(ppi('g4', 'ppi_50_lower'))} to +{pts0(ppi('g4', 'ppi_50_upper'))} points, but the 95% predictive interval admits large negative biases ([[{pts(ppi('g4', 'ppi_95_lower'))}]] points) to large positive biases up to [[{pts(ppi('g4', 'ppi_95_upper'))}]] points."),
  str_glue(
    "Table 4 prints [{table4('t4_g4_ppi95_lower')}, {table4('t4_g4_ppi95_upper')}] for this ",
    "interval. The lower bound in the text is roughly three times the one the table carries."),
  "race_ppi95_lower;race_ppi95_upper",
  ascii_minus(str_glue("{pts(ppi('g4', 'ppi_95_lower'))};{pts(ppi('g4', 'ppi_95_upper'))}")),

  3, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The width of the turnout 95 per cent predictive interval",
  "Results",
  "This uncertainty is also reflected in the very wide predictive intervals: the 50% interval is 13 points wide and the 95% interval is [[45]] points wide.",
  str_glue("This uncertainty is also reflected in the very wide predictive intervals: the 50% interval is {pts0(ppi('g2', 'ppi_50_upper') - ppi('g2', 'ppi_50_lower'))} points wide and the 95% interval is [[{pts(ppi('g2', 'ppi_95_upper') - ppi('g2', 'ppi_95_lower'))}]] points wide."),
  str_glue(
    "Table 4's own interval for turnout is [{table4('t4_g2_ppi95_lower')}, ",
    "{table4('t4_g2_ppi95_upper')}], which is 38 points wide, so the sentence disagrees with ",
    "the table as well as with the data."),
  "turnout_ppi95_width",
  ascii_minus(str_glue("{pts(ppi('g2', 'ppi_95_upper') - ppi('g2', 'ppi_95_lower'))}")),

  4, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The vote buying predictive intervals",
  "Results",
  "In the bottom row of Figure 4a, we show the 50% predictive interval from –14 to [[–2]] points and the 95% predictive interval from [[–27]] to [[+10]] points.",
  str_glue("In the bottom row of Figure 4a, we show the 50% predictive interval from {pts0(ppi('g1', 'ppi_50_lower'))} to [[{pts(ppi('g1', 'ppi_50_upper'))}]] points and the 95% predictive interval from [[{pts(ppi('g1', 'ppi_95_lower'))}]] to [[+{pts(ppi('g1', 'ppi_95_upper'))}]] points."),
  str_glue(
    "Table 4 prints [{table4('t4_g1_ppi50_lower')}, {table4('t4_g1_ppi50_upper')}] and ",
    "[{table4('t4_g1_ppi95_lower')}, {table4('t4_g1_ppi95_upper')}] for the same two ",
    "intervals."),
  "vb_ppi50_upper;vb_ppi95_lower;vb_ppi95_upper",
  ascii_minus(str_glue("{pts(ppi('g1', 'ppi_50_upper'))};{pts(ppi('g1', 'ppi_95_lower'))};{pts(ppi('g1', 'ppi_95_upper'))}")),

  5, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The width of the religious prejudice credible interval",
  "Results",
  "This estimate is in the expected direction, but the credible interval is [[13]] points wide and includes zero.",
  str_glue("This estimate is in the expected direction, but the credible interval is [[{pts(mu('g5', 'ci_upper') - mu('g5', 'ci_lower'))}]] points wide and includes zero."),
  str_glue(
    "Table 4's own interval for religious prejudice is [{table4('t4_g5_ci_lower')}, ",
    "{table4('t4_g5_ci_upper')}], which is 11 points wide."),
  "religion_ci_width",
  ascii_minus(str_glue("{pts(mu('g5', 'ci_upper') - mu('g5', 'ci_lower'))}")),

  6, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The upper bound of the vote buying credible interval",
  "Results",
  "In the top row is the estimated average sensitivity bias across studies for vote-buying questions (black diamond), –8 points with a 95% credible interval stretching from –13 to [[–3]] points.",
  str_glue("In the top row is the estimated average sensitivity bias across studies for vote-buying questions (black diamond), {pts0(mu('g1'))} points with a 95% credible interval stretching from {pts0(mu('g1', 'ci_lower'))} to [[{pts(mu('g1', 'ci_upper'))}]] points."),
  str_glue("Table 4 prints {table4('t4_g1_ci_upper')} for the same bound."),
  "vb_ci_upper",
  ascii_minus(str_glue("{pts(mu('g1', 'ci_upper'))}")),

  7, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The average bias across all underreporting studies",
  "app. p. 16, Section F",
  "Second, as shown in Table 4, the average sensitivity bias in the case of underreporting is [[–3]] points (SE: 1 point).",
  str_glue("Second, as shown in Table 4, the average sensitivity bias in the case of underreporting is [[{pts(mu('g10'))}]] points (SE: {pts0(mu('g10', 'std_error'))} point)."),
  str_glue(
    "Table 4 prints {table4('t4_g10_mu_estimate')}, which rounds to –4 rather than –3 at ",
    "whole-point precision."),
  "appf_under_mu",
  ascii_minus(str_glue("{pts(mu('g10'))}")),

  8, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The lower bound of the racial prejudice credible interval",
  "Results",
  "For questions about racial prejudice, our summary guess is that if anything, subjects overreport racist attitudes by approximately 4 points (95% CI [[–3]] to +9).",
  str_glue("For questions about racial prejudice, our summary guess is that if anything, subjects overreport racist attitudes by approximately 4 points (95% CI [[{pts(mu('g4', 'ci_lower'))}]] to +{pts0(mu('g4', 'ci_upper'))})."),
  str_glue(
    "Table 4 prints {table4('t4_g4_ci_lower')} for the same bound, which is –2 rather than ",
    "–3 at whole-point precision. The estimate the sentence hedges as \"approximately 4 ",
    "points\" is {pts(mu('g4'))} and is correct at the precision it states, so it is left as ",
    "published."),
  "race_ci_lower",
  ascii_minus(str_glue("{pts(mu('g4', 'ci_lower'))}")),

  9, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The lower bound of the authoritarian overreporting predictive interval",
  "Results",
  "Based on 21 studies, our meta-analysis estimate of the average level for studies in which overreporting is predicted is +14 points and the 50% predictive interval suggests a likely level of sensitivity bias between [[+4]] to +24 points.",
  str_glue("Based on {n_studies('g8')} studies, our meta-analysis estimate of the average level for studies in which overreporting is predicted is +{pts0(mu('g8'))} points and the 50% predictive interval suggests a likely level of sensitivity bias between [[+{pts(ppi('g8', 'ppi_50_lower'))}]] to +{pts0(ppi('g8', 'ppi_50_upper'))} points."),
  str_glue("Table 4 prints {table4('t4_g8_ppi50_lower')} for the same bound."),
  "auth_over_ppi50_lower",
  ascii_minus(str_glue("{pts(ppi('g8', 'ppi_50_lower'))}")),

  10, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The sample size at which a list experiment becomes preferable on RMSE grounds",
  "Improving the Power of the List Experiment Design",
  "For a study with 1,000 subjects, the bias must be greater than [[5.5]] points to prefer a list experiment; at 2,000, the bias must be greater than 4 points.",
  str_glue("For a study with 1,000 subjects, the bias must be greater than [[{pts(curve(1000))}]] points to prefer a list experiment; at 2,000, the bias must be greater than {pts0(curve(2000))} points."),
  str_glue(
    "The RMSE indifference curve the article's own Figure 2a plots crosses at ",
    "{pts2(curve(1000))} points at this sample size, so a bias of 5.5 points would not in ",
    "fact prefer the list experiment. The companion bound at 2,000 subjects crosses at ",
    "{pts2(curve(2000))} and holds as stated."),
  "fig2a_rmse_n1000",
  ascii_minus(str_glue("{pts(curve(1000))}")),

  11, "description", "pipeline", "full",
  "Only one of the two sexual orientation estimates has an unexpected sign",
  "Results",
  "[[These estimates both have]] an unexpected sign relative to the [[predictions and are not]] distinguishable from zero.",
  "[[Only the overreporting estimate has]] an unexpected sign relative to the [[predictions, and neither is]] distinguishable from zero.",
  str_glue(
    "The sentence follows directly from the misstated figure corrected above. ",
    "Underreporting predicts a negative difference between the direct question and the list ",
    "experiment, and the underreporting average is {pts(mu('g7'))} points, which is the sign ",
    "predicted. Overreporting predicts a positive difference, and the overreporting average ",
    "is {pts(mu('g6'))} points, which is not. Both credible intervals contain zero, so the ",
    "second half of the sentence stands as published."),
  "so_unexpected_sign",
  NA_character_,

  12, "label", "reading", "brief",
  "A misspelling in the label of Figure 3(a)",
  "p. 1305, panel (a) of Figure 3",
  "[[Difference-in-prevalance]]",
  "[[Difference-in-prevalence]]",
  "The figure's own caption and Note spell the word correctly; the panel label is the only place it does not.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  13, "label", "reading", "brief",
  "Figure 4(c) labels the racial prejudice studies with the wrong prediction",
  "p. 1308, panel (c) of Figure 4",
  "Racial prejudice ([[overreporting]])",
  "Racial prejudice ([[underreporting]])",
  "Table 4 lists the racial prejudice studies under Underreporting and has no overreporting row for them, and every other panel of the figure is labelled with the prediction its row of Table 4 carries.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  14, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "The Tourangeau and Yan reference prints a first page in place of a page range",
  "p. 1315, refs",
  "Psychological Bulletin 133 (5): [[859]].",
  "Psychological Bulletin 133 (5): [[859--83]].",
  "Crossref, doi 10.1037/0033-2909.133.5.859, gives the article's pages as 859 to 883. The corrected range keeps the reference list's own style, which drops the leading digits a last page shares with the first.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  15, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "The Yu, Tian and Tang reference prints a first page in place of a page range",
  "p. 1315, refs",
  "Metrika 67: [[251]].",
  "Metrika 67: [[251--63]].",
  "Crossref, doi 10.1007/s00184-007-0131-x, gives the article's pages as 251 to 263. The corrected range keeps the reference list's own style.",
  "",
  NA_character_
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids, corrected_values),
                as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

# Only what is marked has changed. Outside the marks a corrected sentence must read exactly
# as the page prints it, so a figure an entry does not correct, recomputed from the deposit,
# has to reproduce the published token. A mismatch here is either a figure that needs its
# own entry or a mark that does not cover what the entry changes.
unmarked <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[.*?\\]\\]", "[[]]")
stopifnot(unmarked(entries$published) == unmarked(entries$corrected))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
# The column and the sentence are written from one expression, so they begin in agreement
# and this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span
# to another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its
# value. Each value has to be inside the span it belongs to, matched by position where the
# counts line up, and inside SOME span where an entry marks a label as well as a number and
# its spans outnumber its values.
marked_spans <- function(x) ascii_minus(str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2])

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values)) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

value_placed <- pmap_lgl(quantified, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, \(v, s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))))
  }
})

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# The placement is written to the spine as values_in_spans, one logical per entry: TRUE when
# every corrected value is the token its sentence prints, NA for an entry with no values. The
# gate above stops on FALSE, because no entry here stores a value on the claim's scale rather
# than the sentence's.
entries <- entries |>
  left_join(tibble(entry = quantified$entry, values_in_spans = value_placed), by = "entry")

# An entry that changes a quantity has to say which one, and an entry that changes none may
# not carry a value. The class is the declaration and this is where it binds. A note-form
# entry corrects nothing, so it carries NA whatever its class. An empty claim_ids is stored
# as "" and counts as missing here.
has_ids <- !is.na(entries$claim_ids) & entries$claim_ids != ""
needs_value <- entries$class == "quantity" & entries$form != "note" & has_ids
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[needs_value])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[!needs_value])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | has_ids)
)

# Every id an entry claims to correct must be a real ground-truth claim. The build gate in
# ground_truth/build_ground_truth.R checks the same property from the other side; checking it
# here too means a dangling id cannot survive a render.
gt_ids <- read_csv(here("ground_truth", "blair_coppock_moor_2020_ground_truth.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE)$claim_id
cited_ids <- entries$claim_ids |>
  str_split(";") |>
  unlist() |>
  str_trim() |>
  discard(\(x) is.na(x) | x == "")
stopifnot(all(cited_ids %in% gt_ids))

# The prose below counts the entries in words, as the note has always done.
n_entries_word <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine",
                    "ten", "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen", "fourteen", "fifteen")[nrow(entries)]

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
```

This note lists `r n_entries_word` corrections to "When to Worry about Sensitivity Bias: A Social Reference Theory and Evidence from 30 Years of List Experiments," published in the *American Political Science Review* 114(4), doi [10.1017/S0003055420000374](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0003055420000374): ten misstated numbers, one sentence that describes the estimates incorrectly as a result, two misprinted figure labels, and two page ranges in the reference list printed as a first page alone. **None of them changes a conclusion of the paper.** Ten are in the article's text, two are in its figures, two are in its reference list, and one, entry 7, is in its online appendix. Entries 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 11 restate a quantity the article also prints in Table 4, and in each case Table 4 is right and the sentence is not. The sentences that carry the paper's findings, and Table 4 itself, are unaffected.

Every number in a corrected sentence below is computed from the deposited replication archive ([10.7910/DVN/YUXHZT](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/YUXHZT)) at the time this document is rendered, including the numbers that were not wrong. The code and output supporting each correction are at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/blair_coppock_moor_2020](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/blair_coppock_moor_2020).

**Bold marks the corrections, and only what is bold has changed.** Everything else in a corrected sentence reads exactly as the page prints it, figures included. A figure an entry does not correct is recomputed from the deposit like every other, then stated at the article's own precision, usually whole points; each one reproduces the published figure, and this document refuses to render if one does not. A corrected figure is stated to one decimal place, so a correction smaller than a point can be seen at all. Where the fuller value of an uncorrected figure matters it is given in the note beneath the entry.

The first six entries are substantive: the number a reader would quote is wrong by more than a point, and the first two turn on a sign. Entries 6 to 10 differ from the article's own figure, in Table 4 or for entry 10 in Figure 2a, by less than a point, which is exactly why they need a decimal to be visible at all. Entries 12 and 13 are panel labels: a misspelling in Figure 3, and a panel of Figure 4 that names the wrong prediction. The last two were found by an audit that sends every printed reference entry whole to Crossref and checks the authoritative record back into it.

```{r render-entries, results="asis"}
# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, so every emitted entry opens
# with one.
walk(seq_len(nrow(entries)), function(i) {
  e <- entries[i, ]
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\n> ", bold(e$published),
      "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
})
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else that
# carries these corrections reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot drift.
# The spine's vocabularies are closed (cleanup of 2026-11-07): a value outside them is a
# typo, and the edition builders read these columns to shape every entry.
stopifnot(
  all(entries$class %in% c("quantity", "description", "interpretation", "definition", "label", "float", "cross_reference", "wording", "spelling", "typography", "bibliographic")),
  all(entries$form %in% c("full", "brief", "note")),
  all(entries$source %in% c("pipeline", "reading", "reference_audit", "publisher_record", "authors_archive", "proof"))
)
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
